items.title: Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline for Multi-Instance Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: We present the Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline (ASP), an offline rollout scheduler for multi-instance asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) of large language models (LLMs). ASP jointly reduces three sources of rollout underutilization - padding bubbles from intra-minibatch length
items.editor_note: Infra angle: a rollout scheduler that removes padding and other underutilization in asynchronous LLM RL.

items.title: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
items.summary_1line: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation

items.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories. However, despite this progress,...
items.editor_note: Encodes memory into world models with test-time model-based RL.

items.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement lea...
items.editor_note: Uses RL to learn incremental summaries as bounded memory of unbounded histories.

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary_1line: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, s...
items.editor_note: AI-generated scaffolds to use more of RLVR experience than a single outcome reward.

items.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
items.summary_1line: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on
items.editor_note: Interpretability for deep RL policies with many simultaneous actions.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning: Optimizing 0.6B Dense Models on TPU v7 via vLLM
items.summary_1line: Co-designing RL for a Qwen3-0.6B dense policy on Google Cloud TPU v7 across vLLM, Tunix, MaxText, and Pallas, with a 107x end-to-end speedup from ~100 minutes to ~56 seconds per true-8K RL cycle.
items.editor_note: Only practitioner item: vLLM reports ~100 min to ~56 s per 8K RL cycle for Qwen3-0.6B on TPU v7.

items.title: StateAlign: Internalizing State-Aware Decision-Making for Reliable Multi-Turn Tool Agents via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Reinforcement learning has improved the tool-use capabilities of large language models. However, better task performance can coincide with increased tool hallucination. Reliable tool use requires decisions to follow t...
items.editor_note: Failure mode named: RL tool-use gains can come with more tool hallucination; trains state-aware decisions.

items.title: Learn then Bet: Learning Interpretable Rules for Reliable Agent Intervention
items.summary_1line: Autonomous agents now run for hundreds of steps with little or no human supervision. In practice, practitioners use runtime monitors such as turn limits and keyword filters to decide when a run should be stopped, upgraded, or assisted. However, these heuristics may stop runs that
items.editor_note: Replaces turn limits and keyword filters with learned, interpretable rules for when to stop or assist an agent run.

items.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is one of the most promising paths toward an AI singularity for superintelligence. Achieving this vision requires AI systems to undertake the full training pipeline for iterative impro...
items.editor_note: Multi-agent system that attempts to run the RL training pipeline itself.

items.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible f...
items.editor_note: Extends demonstration bootstrapping from single-agent to multi-agent RL.

items.title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
items.summary_1line: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills. Planning such behaviors efficiently is challenging: given a library of parameterized skills, solutions lie in a vast
items.editor_note: Learned skill-effect world models to speed long-horizon manipulation planning.

items.title: Algorithm Distillation for Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Safe in-context reinforcement learning (Safe ICRL) asks a policy with fixed parameters to improve on an unseen constrained task from its interaction history while aiming to keep its cost within a budget. Prior work st...
items.editor_note: Safety angle: in-context RL that improves on new tasks while staying within a cost budget.

items.title: RLDE: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Interpretable Iterative Document Editing
items.summary_1line: Improving the quality, clarity, and flow of long documents remains a challenging problem in NLP, as human editing typically occurs through iterative refinement rather than a single-pass rewrite. Most existing automate...
items.editor_note: Applied RL: iterative, interpretable document editing instead of one-pass rewrites.

items.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) requires models to acquire new capabilities while retaining performance on previous tasks. A stability-oriented perspective common in conventional continual learning emphasizes knowledge preservation and interference mitigation. Complementin
items.editor_note: Continual RL via replay guided by policy improvement, not only knowledge preservation.

items.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
items.summary_1line: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and tim...
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, evaluation.
items.editor_note: Diagnostic benchmark separating reasoning, physical action and their composition in manipulation.

items.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Continual reinforcement learning requires agents to adapt when the task changes while reusing what they know about the environment. Successor features separate dynamics from task-specific reward, but their effectiveness depends on the choice of base features. Taking the identific
items.editor_note: Grid-cell-inspired successor features as a reusable basis when tasks change.

items.title: CTRL: Concurrent Training and Rollout for LLM Reinforcement Learning via GPU Co-Residency
items.summary_1line: CTRL is a system that runs an RL learner and a persistent rollout engine on every GPU under CUDA MPS, reporting 1.11-2.24× the throughput of verl's asynchronous baselines across 24 Qwen3 workload settings.
items.editor_note: Systems angle: learner and rollout engine share each GPU under CUDA MPS, reporting 1.11-2.24x verl async throughput.

items.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
items.summary_1line: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of e
items.editor_note: Video world models trained on motion regions to evaluate robot policies more faithfully.

items.title: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models
items.summary_1line: Proposes LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual reinforcement learning framework that uses latent world models instead of large image or video generators to improve pretrained vision-language-action robot policies, tested on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real ALOHA robot.
items.editor_note: Swaps image/video generators for latent world models to make robot-policy RL rollouts cheaper.

items.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of...
items.editor_note: Turns formal strategy-logic specifications into shaped rewards for multi-agent RL.

items.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use
items.summary_1line: Proposes AOVO, a data-centric reinforcement learning framework that teaches multimodal LLMs when to use visual tools by reweighting training questions with perception attribution, without tool-specific rewards.
items.editor_note: Teaches visual tool use by reweighting training questions instead of engineering tool-specific rewards.

items.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
items.summary_1line: Proposes State-Verified Reinforcement Learning, which trains tutoring agents using a deterministic verifier of workspace state changes; after training, Qwen3.8-27B's strict success on a 60-task benchmark rises from 51.47% to 80.74%.
items.editor_note: Reward from a deterministic verifier of workspace state changes; reports 51.47% to 80.74% strict success.

items.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
items.summary_1line: Introduces RoboTrack, a benchmark of 307 human-annotated real robot manipulation videos and a 15M-track synthetic training dataset built on MolmoSpaces, for point tracking in robotics.
items.editor_note: Point-tracking benchmark of 307 annotated real robot videos plus a 15M-track synthetic set.

items.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
items.summary_1line: CO-GRAFT is a framework that attributes RL gains in Search-R1 search agents to four functional roles by mixing RL-trained and pre-RL policies, finding query generation contributes at most 15% of the gain.
items.editor_note: Attributes RL gains to agent roles and finds query generation contributes at most 15%.

items.title: Avalon-M1: Reinforcement Learning from Collective Rewards
items.summary_1line: Introduces RLCR, a training method where a CEO model and up to eight specialists share one policy and are trained on a common outcome-based advantage, with results reported across 12 benchmarks and safety tests on the 120B Avalon-M1-Mini.
items.editor_note: Trains a CEO model and up to eight specialists on one shared outcome-based advantage.

items.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
items.summary_1line: Proposes RLVB, a reinforcement learning method that rewards AI agents for gathering more evidence while several answers remain possible and for committing once evidence suffices, using a simulator-computed posterior rather than a judge or outcome reward.
items.editor_note: Rewards agents for gathering evidence until a simulator-computed posterior says to commit, with no judge model.

items.title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary_1line: Introduces WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for robotic manipulation that compares candidate actions within shared latent physics, paired with a planning method (CAP) that ranks plans by advantage over an incumbent.
items.editor_note: Counterfactual world model that ranks robot plans by advantage over an incumbent.

items.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
items.summary_1line: Researchers study whether LLM-based coding agents can write control policies by reading an environment's source code as a readable world model, and report that these policies match or beat conventional RL with far less experience.
items.editor_note: Challenges the premise: coding agents reading environment source match or beat RL with far less experience.

items.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
items.summary_1line: Proposes Maco-RL, a mixed-task reinforcement learning method that trains one policy across domains, raising Qwen3.5-27B's overall score on five benchmarks from 43.6 to 60.1.
items.editor_note: Newest: one mixed-task RL policy raises Qwen3.5-27B from 43.6 to 60.1 across five benchmarks.

editorial.tldr: This is a theme thread of mostly arXiv papers, not one developing story. Since Nov 6 it has tracked RL for agents (multi-agent training, RL-learned memory, rollout cost), the finding that RL tool-use gains can raise tool hallucination, and Nov 23 work tracing gains to verified state and specific agent roles.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 25: a paper reports coding agents that read an environment's source code write policies matching or beating conventional RL, and Maco-RL lifts Qwen3.5-27B from 43.6 to 60.1 on five benchmarks with mixed-task RL.
editorial.why_it_matters: If you post-train or operate tool-using agents, this cluster names where RL pays off and what it costs: rollout throughput, tool hallucination, reward design, and when code-writing agents can skip RL, though nearly every result is author-reported.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before funding an RL run for an agent, test whether a coding agent can write the policy from your environment's code, and score any RL-tuned model on tool-hallucination rate and per-role behavior next to task success.

beats.summary: The ASP rollout scheduler, vLLM's 107x TPU v7 cycle speedup, CTRL's learner/rollout co-residency, and latent world-model rollouts for VLA policies.

beats.headline: Better task scores can mean more tool hallucination, so papers add state-awareness, scaffolds and stop rules
beats.summary: AutoScaffold, StateAlign, Learn then Bet intervention rules, and safe in-context RL under a cost budget.

beats.headline: Applied RL papers ride along on shared vocabulary
beats.summary: ReShap interpretability for multi-action policies and RLDE iterative document editing.

beats.headline: Continual RL: learning new tasks without losing old ones
beats.summary: Policy-improvement-guided replay and grid cells as spectral successor features.

beats.headline: Robot-learning benchmarks and world models join the thread
beats.summary: ToyBlocks, Mind2Act World and RoboTrack benchmarks, plus Lazy-MOSAIC, motion-region video world models and WhatIf counterfactual planning; adjacent to agent RL rather than part of it.

beats.headline: Where RL gains come from in tool-using agents: verified state, data reweighting, role attribution
beats.summary: AOVO drops tool-specific rewards, state-verified RL trains tutoring agents against a deterministic checker, and CO-GRAFT splits Search-R1 gains by role.

beats.headline: New reward signals and mixed-task training, while one paper asks whether RL is needed at all
beats.summary: RLCR shared-outcome rewards for CEO-plus-specialist agents, RLVB belief-based rewards, Maco-RL mixed-task training, and coding agents that write policies from environment source.

open_questions: Does StateAlign's reduction in tool hallucination hold on tool APIs outside the paper's own benchmarks?
Does vLLM's 107x RL cycle speedup on TPU v7 carry over to policies larger than Qwen3-0.6B?
Does CTRL's 1.11-2.24x throughput over verl's async baselines show up in an independent reproduction?
If query generation explains at most 15% of Search-R1's RL gain, which role carries the rest, and does the split hold for other search agents?
Do code-written policies keep matching RL when the environment's source code is unavailable or too large to read?
Does Maco-RL's 43.6 to 60.1 gain from one mixed-task policy hold against per-domain RL at equal compute?
